title: Abroad, India’s RSS Speaks of ‘Love.’ At Home, Its Affiliates Attack Christians.
gist: Since the BJP won West Bengal in May 2026, RSS-linked groups such as the VHP, Bajrang Dal, Hindu Jagran Manch and Shree Ram Janmotsab Samity have repeatedly disrupted Christian house-church prayer gatherings, even as RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat preached 'pure love' and unity on a centenary tour of New York, Toronto and London; Christians (0.72% of the state) have suspended house meetings in several districts.

insights.claim: On August 26, 2026, Hindu supremacist activists disrupted a Bible-study house fellowship of about 50 people, many of them Hindus, at Goutam Bera's residence in Ranichak village, Sutahata, West Bengal, livestreaming the raid on Facebook.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Illustrates how social media amplifies communal vigilantism in newly BJP-governed states.

insights.claim: After the Sutahata raid, police took 17 prayer attendees including the pastor for medical checks and then interrogated them and examined their phones at the police station, rather than acting against the attackers.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Police treating victims as suspects signals weak rule-of-law protection for religious minorities under the new state government.

insights.claim: Attackers at Sutahata openly identified themselves with the VHP and the Shree Ram Janmotsab Samity, a group that openly advertises RSS and VHP events on its Facebook page.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Direct organizational links undercut BJP claims that such incidents are isolated.

insights.claim: A VHP-linked participant urged viewers to beat Christian organizers with brooms, calling them worse than terrorists, while the Samity warned of 'severe consequences' for those spreading Christianity.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Explicit incitement heightens reputational and human-rights risk for India's image abroad.
insights.quote: Beat them up with brooms whenever and wherever you see them. They are worse than terrorists.

insights.claim: Senior BJP leader Amit Malviya described the Sutahata incident and two others as 'isolated local objections to prayer gatherings… peacefully resolved by the police', a characterization contradicted by attackers' own social-media videos.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Official downplaying of communal incidents is a pattern to discount when assessing India's minority-rights risk.

insights.claim: A recent database described the RSS family of organizations, the Sangh Parivar, as 'the largest far-right network in history', while Narendra Modi calls the RSS the world's largest NGO.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Divergent framing of the RSS is central to how foreign governments and investors perceive India's governance and ESG risk.
insights.quote: the largest far-right network in history
insights.locator: Its based on actions like these

insights.claim: During its centenary tour of New York, Toronto and London, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said 'pure and divine love' is the basis of RSS work and described diversity as a 'decoration for our innate unity' that must be respected and protected.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: The RSS is running an international image campaign; its credibility depends on domestic conduct that contradicts it.
insights.quote: I heard some people say intense hatred is the basis of our work. It is just the reverse.
insights.locator: During a September 6 event in London

insights.claim: The day after Mohan Bhagwat's August 29 Madison Square Garden speech on oneness, RSS-linked activists disrupted three separate Christian prayer gatherings in West Bengal.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: The gap between diaspora-facing messaging and domestic action is a reputational risk the article documents in detail.
insights.locator: In West Bengal, the next day

insights.claim: Between August 23 and September 12, 2026, Bajrang Dal, VHP and Hindu Jagran Manch activists carried out numerous disruptions of churches, house prayers and a Christian-run school across Howrah, South 24 Parganas and North 24 Parganas districts.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Frequency and geographic spread indicate an organized campaign rather than isolated events.
insights.locator: Here are some of the incidents

insights.claim: On September 1, Hindu Jagran Manch, an RSS affiliate, locked up a Christian-run school at Hasnabad in North 24 Parganas district, objecting to Jesus imagery and teaching about Jesus.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Targeting of Christian-run educational institutions threatens a sector where Christians play an outsized role in West Bengal.

insights.claim: Anti-Christian attacks are completely new in West Bengal and began soon after the BJP defeated the Trinamool Congress in the May 2026 state election, ending its 15-year rule.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: State-level regime change can rapidly shift minority security conditions; relevant for political-risk monitoring in BJP-won states.

insights.claim: Anti-Christian hostility has surged in several Indian states, especially BJP-ruled ones, since Narendra Modi, himself an RSS volunteer, came to power in 2014.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: A long-running national trend now extending to new states; persistent social-stability and reputational risk.

insights.claim: Christian community members describe the situation as a 'Sunday horror show', with one or more incidents every Sunday over the past four months.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Weekly regularity indicates sustained, not episodic, pressure on minorities.
insights.quote: It has become a Sunday horror show. Over the past four months, there have been one or more incidents every Sunday
insights.locator: It has become a Sunday horror show

insights.claim: An attacker at Sutahata explicitly tied the raid to the change in state government, saying the targets were propagating other religions 'even after the change in the [state] government'.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Perpetrators perceive political cover from the new government, suggesting incidents will continue absent state pushback.

insights.claim: Most attacks target informal house churches in areas without formal churches; CPI(M) state secretary Mohammed Salim argues this low-intensity approach terrorizes poor Christians while avoiding international headlines that attacks on prominent churches would draw.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Deliberately below-the-radar tactics mean headline indicators may understate minority-rights deterioration.
insights.quote: They know attacks on prominent churches can become major news abroad

insights.claim: Christians, just 0.72 percent of West Bengal's population per the 2011 Census, have suspended house prayer meetings in several districts as a result of the attacks.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Measurable retreat from religious practice is a concrete indicator of eroding religious freedom.
insights.locator: The list has since kept growing

insights.claim: According to the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, police complaints have been filed in only a few incidents because victims fear legal action, and police have detained and harassed victims instead of apprehending attackers.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Underreporting means official crime data will understate the scale of communal incidents.
insights.locator: Incidents are many, but police complaints

insights.claim: Christian community leaders are publicly appealing to Mohan Bhagwat's overseas messages of love, hoping the RSS-led ruling apparatus will enforce coexistence on the ground and planning to petition the state minority welfare minister.
insights.speaker: Snigdhendu Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Minority groups are using the RSS's international messaging as leverage; watch for any state government response.
insights.locator: Herod Mullick, secretary of the Bangiya
